extracted.intended_audience: federal agency staff administering or overseeing Federal advisory committees (FACs); legal/compliance advisors; public stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and statutory/regulatory standards governing the establishment, operation, oversight, and termination of Federal advisory committees (FACs), and related requirements affecting public access and agency procedures. Useful for agency officials ensuring FACs comply with FACA, implementing regulations, OMB guidance, Executive Orders, and UMRA exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑FACA guidance and early Executive Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Justice guidelines in 1955; a bill in 1957 that did not pass Congress; Bureau of the Budget guidance in the early 1960s; and an Executive Order in 1962.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These historical actions represent early attempts to regulate advisory committees and provide context for later statutory regulation. (Text: "Attempts to regulate advisory committees included Department of Justice guidelines in 1955; a bill in 1957 that did not make it out of Congress; Bureau of the Budget (predecessor to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB)) guidance in the early 1960’s; and an Executive Order in 1962.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) — core statutory framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) formalizes a process for establishing, operating, overseeing, and terminating Federal advisory committees (FACs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FACA provides the statutory requirements and legislative history that explain the Act’s language and rationale. Agencies must follow the Act’s processes when creating or managing FACs. (Text: "The Federal Advisory Committee Act formalizes a process for establishing, operating, overseeing, and terminating Federal advisory committees (FACs). The Act’s legislative history provides the rationale behind the language in the Act.")

rubrics_metrics.name: FACA Final Rule — implementing regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations promulgated to provide the details for implementing the Federal Advisory Committee Act are known as the FACA Final Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Rule contains the detailed regulatory requirements agencies must follow to implement FACA; it operationalizes the Act’s statutory provisions. (Text: "Regulations have been promulgated that provide the details for implementing the Act and are known as the FACA Final Rule.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Government in the Sunshine Act (5 U.S.C. 552b) — public access and closure exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the Government in the Sunshine Act is to provide information regarding the decision‑making process of the federal government to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act also enumerates situations when the President and federal agencies can close FAC meetings to the public, setting limits on non‑public meetings and defining allowable exemptions. (Text: "The purpose of the Act is to provide information regarding the decision-making process of the federal government to the public. This Act also lists situations when the President and federal agencies can close FAC meetings to the public.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12024 — delegation of Presidential FACA functions to GSA
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 12024 (Transfer of Certain Advisory Committee Functions, 1977) delegated to the Administrator of General Services all the functions vested in the President by the Federal Advisory Committee Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This delegation centralizes certain FACA responsibilities in GSA; agencies should be aware of GSA’s delegated role under this Order. (Text: "This Executive Order delegated to the Administrator of General Services all the functions vested in the President by the Federal Advisory Committee Act.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12838 — termination and limitation of FACs; justification for new committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 12838 (1993) reduced the number of discretionary FACs by one‑third and required compelling justification for any new discretionary FACs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies creating new discretionary advisory committees must provide compelling justification; existing discretionary FACs were subject to reduction under this Order. (Text: "This Executive Order reduced the number of discretionary FACs at the time by one-third, and required compelling justification for any new discretionary FACs.")

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular No. A‑135 — committee planning and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular No. A‑135 (1994) provides guidance and instructions on managing FACs and requires executive departments and agencies to establish a committee planning and review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must implement committee planning and review processes as directed by OMB Circular A‑135 to ensure appropriate oversight and management of FACs. (Text: "This Circular provides guidance and instructions on managing FACs and requires executive departments and agencies to establish a committee planning and review process.")

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 204 of Public Law 104‑4 (UMRA) — exemption for communications with state/local/tribal governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 204 of the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) provides a critical exemption to the Federal Advisory Committee Act to promote free communication between the federal government and state, local, and tribal governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where Section 204 applies, communications with state, local, and tribal governments may be exempt from certain FACA requirements; agencies should consult UMRA and OMB guidelines/instructions for implementing Section 204 to determine applicability. (Text: "UMRA provides a critical exemption to the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA), in order to promote the free communication between the federal government and state, local, and tribal governments. More details on what it means and whether or not the exemption applies to a particular situation can be found at UMRA. Access OMB guidelines and instructions for implementing Section 204.")
